newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-STRANG HITS DEBUT HALF-CENTURY FOR KENT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STRANG HITS DEBUT HALF-CENTURY FOR KENT.

text.p: Kent's Zimbabwe leg-spinner Paul Strang helped his new county into a winning position but with the bat rather than the ball in their opening county championship match against Derbyshire at Canterbury on Friday.
Strang, out without scoring in Kent's first innings 251 and wicketless as Derby replied with 248, smacked an aggressive 69 at a run a ball as Kent made 333 in their second innings.
The Zimbabwean was particularly severe on ex-England fast bowler Devon Malcolm who, after taking six wickets in the first innings, managed only one for 112 in the second.
Derby, needing 337 to win, finished the third day on 59 for two and with two of their players injured will be hard-pressed to avoid defeat on the final day.

Andy Hayhurst tore a cartilage in his right knee after falling awkwardly while fielding and Phil DeFreitas, after recording his best figures for the county of seven for 64, left the field with a recurrence of a groin injury.
Derby's best hope of avoiding defeat appeared to lie with the weather which hit all the county matches on Friday. No play was possible in three of them and the others were severly curtailed.
At Chelmsford only 50 minutes of play was possible but Essex all-rounder Ronnie Irani did his England test hopes no harm as he took his innings to a career-best 123 not out against Hampshire.
It enabled captain Paul Prichard to declare at 442 for eight and set Hampshire an awesome 528 to win. But when they had reached three without loss, rain ended play for the day.
